LEIDEN UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER | 15 February 2025 | Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation for suspected prostate cancer. PSA 187.0 ng/mL, prior biopsy Positive.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 57.28 mL in total volume. A discrete abnormality resides in the right peripheral zone, spanning the base to mid segment, with dimensions of roughly 24 x 18 x 20 mm. T2-weighted sequences show marked hypointensity and poorly circumscribed borders. Diffusion-weighted imaging confirms restricted movement, mirrored by low ADC signal. Dynamic contrast enhancement highlights early, focal uptake. Seminal vesicles appear symmetric and normal. There is no evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Pelvic lymph nodes remain unremarkable in size. The visualized skeleton lacks suspicious osseous changes.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. PSAD 3.26 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.964853.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: A January 2024 assay recorded a prostate-specific antigen level of 134.0 ng/mL, triggering an expedited urology referral for comprehensive assessment. Subsequent transrectal ultrasound-guided sampling yielded confirmed adenocarcinoma. Specialist surveillance has continued since that initial diagnosis, and a fresh measurement of 187.0 ng/mL accompanies this current review. Laboratory panels and renal parameters remain within stable limits.
